description:
This merge proposal adds autopkgtests with the purpose of guarding against
the most common modes of failures in rust-coreutils uploads. It includes the
following tests:

* all-utils: Run resolution + smoke + curated functional tests for every util.
  If a test fails, but the util is redirected to GNU, it will be reported as
  FAIL (REDIRECTED) and will not cause the test to fail. Only failures on
  active rust-coreutils utils count as real failures.

* arg-parity: Run different argument flag combinations and compare the behavior
  between rust-coreutils and GNU. If a test differs between them, it fails.
  It is possible to add exceptions to known mismatches that either have a known
  bug or are considered as "won't fix". These tests can be marked as
  KNOWN MISMATCH with a comment specifying the reason why, which allows the
  test suite to still pass.

* behavior-parity: Compare behavioral edge cases (rust vs. GNU) that other
  tools like initramfs-tools, debhelper, etc. rely on. These include for
  instance the `install` idiom (`install --mode NNN /dev/null FILE`,
  `install -d`, `install -D`) used in postinst scripts, as well as
  `realpath`/`readlink` flag handling relied on by initramfs-tools
  hook-functions.

* format-parity: Compare output format strings (rust vs. GNU) where other tools
  parse coreutils output. This includes tools like `stat -c`, `printf`, and
  `md5sum`.

* pipeline-parity: Compare pipeline behavior (rust vs. GNU). This includes
  cases such as SIGPIPE handling (LP: #2134578, #2133156, #2125943) and
  NUL-separated pipelines.

* regression-lp: Test for specific Launchpad bug fixes referenced in
  `debian/changelog`. Each test case is named after its LP number (e.g.
  `LP #2134578: tee with multiple --append`), which makes it easier to
  audit the suite against the changelog. This is especially useful if a patch
  gets functionally altered, either intentionally or by mistake.

* system-build-sed: Build the sed package using rust-coreutils. This test
  aims to exercise the coreutils' capacity to handle builds as a first line
  of defense against FTBFS. Because rust-coreutils is built using its
  *previous* version (Rust bootstraps itself), these bugs were only noticed
  in other packages' build processes.

  In order to guard against test failures where the error lies in the sed
  package itself, the autopkgtest is run in phases. First, sed is built without
  tests using rust-coreutils. If that fails, the build will retry with GNU. If
  building with GNU fails, then the test will exit 1 and print the build log
  tail, as it is inconclusive what the error is.

  The second phase runs the sed test-suite against rust-coreutils
  (make check - no rebuild). If that succeeds, the autopkgtest passes and
  exits 0. If it fails, it will move on to the third phase which instead runs
  GNU as a baseline. Contrary to the first phase, the autopkgtest passes if
  both rust-coreutils and GNU fail the sed test-suite.

  This test requires `needs-root`, `isolation-machine` and `breaks-testbed`,
  as it modifies apt sources and `/usr/bin/` symlinks. Symlink restoration
  is guaranteed via `trap ... EXIT`, so the testbed is always restored to
  rust-coreutils even on failure.

The suite is data-driven: `all-utils` and `arg-parity` use generic runner
scripts with per-util configuration sourced from separate `-data` files
(`all-utils-data`, `arg-parity-data`). Shared helpers (resolution, parity
comparison, known-mismatch handling, symlink management for baseline
comparison) live in `debian/tests/common`, which is sourced by all tests.
See `debian/tests/README` for an in-depth description of the test suite,
including how to add new test cases and how to run the tests locally.

+# rust-coreutils autopkgtests
+
+This directory contains the autopkgtest suite for the `rust-coreutils` package.
+These tests verify that rust-coreutils works correctly as the **system
+coreutils** — i.e., when it replaces GNU coreutils at `/usr/bin/<util>` via
+the `coreutils-from-uutils` symlink layer.
+
+## Why these tests exist
+
+rust-coreutils is a drop-in replacement for GNU coreutils. On systems where
+the transition is active, every other package's build process, maintainer
+scripts, and system boot depend on rust-coreutils behaving identically to
+GNU. A subtle bug in `cp`, `mv`, `install`, or any other util can FTBFS
+hundreds of packages or break system operation.
+
+These tests are designed to catch regressions **before** they reach the
+archive, covering:
+
+- Basic functionality of every utility (smoke + curated functional tests)
+- Argument combination behavior vs GNU coreutils (flag parity testing)
+- Output format compatibility for tools that parse coreutils output
+  (stat, printf, md5sum format strings)
+- Behavioral edge cases that system tools depend on (install idioms,
+  realpath/readlink, tsort)
+- Pipeline behavior (SIGPIPE handling, NUL-separated pipelines)
+- Specific bugs fixed in past releases (regression tests)
+- The ability of real packages to build under rust-coreutils (system build
+  tests)
+
+## Test overview
+
+| Test | What it does | Runtime |
+|------|--------------|---------|
+| `all-utils` | Resolution + smoke (`--version`/`--help`) + curated functional test for every util in `rust-coreutils.hardlinks`. GNU-redirected utils (e.g. `cp`, `df`) are tested against the rust-coreutils binary directly — failures are reported as `FAIL (REDIRECTED)` and don't fail the test | ~5 sec |
+| `arg-parity` | Compares rust-coreutils vs GNU coreutils for flag combinations (singles + pairs + curated cases) | ~15 sec |
+| `format-parity` | Compares output format strings: `stat -c` specifiers, `printf` formats/escapes, `md5sum` output format | ~3 sec |
+| `behavior-parity` | Compares behavioral edge cases: `install` idiom, `realpath`/`readlink` flags, `tsort` ordering | ~3 sec |
+| `pipeline-parity` | Compares pipeline behavior: SIGPIPE handling (downstream exits early), NUL-separated pipelines | ~3 sec |
+| `regression-lp` | Pinned tests for specific Launchpad bug fixes referenced in `debian/changelog` | ~1 sec |
+| `system-build-sed` | Builds `sed` from source with rust-coreutils as system coreutils, with GNU baseline comparison on failure | ~2 min |
+
+## File structure
+
+```
+debian/tests/
+    control                 # autopkgtest stanza declarations (deps, restrictions)
+    common                  # shared shell helpers (sourced by all tests)
+    README                  # this file
+    all-utils               # generic runner: resolution + smoke + functional tests
+    all-utils-data          # per-util functional test cases (human-edited)
+    arg-parity              # generic runner: flag combination parity testing
+    arg-parity-data         # per-util flag lists + curated cases + known issues
+    format-parity           # output format parity: stat, printf, md5sum
+    behavior-parity         # behavioral parity: install idiom, realpath, tsort
+    pipeline-parity         # pipeline parity: SIGPIPE, NUL-separated
+    regression-lp           # LP bug regression tests
+    system-build-sed        # sed build test with conditional GNU baseline
+```
+
+## Data-driven design
+
+`all-utils` and `arg-parity` use a **data-driven** pattern: the runner script
+is generic (rarely changed), and all per-util configuration lives in a
+separate `-data` file that is sourced at runtime. This keeps test logic
+separate from test data, making both easier to maintain.
+
+`format-parity`, `behavior-parity`, and `pipeline-parity` are self-contained
+scripts with clearly commented sections per area. Each test case is explicit
+and documented — no auto-generation.
+
+### `all-utils-data`
+
+Each util has a case in a single `case` statement:
+
+```sh
+echo)
+    [ "$("$bin" hello)" = "hello" ] ;;
+```
+
+- `$bin` — the resolved binary path (may be `/usr/bin/<util>` or
+  `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/<util>`)
+- `$t` — a per-util temp directory (already created)
+- Return 0 = pass, 1 = fail, 77 = skip (preconditions not met)
+
+**To add a test case:** add another assertion to the existing case (chain
+with `&&`).
+
+**To add a new util:** add a case to the switch. The runner auto-discovers
+utils from `debian/rust-coreutils.hardlinks`.
+
+### `arg-parity-data`
+
+Each util is configured with:
+
+```sh
+arg_parity_setup <util> <mode> <flags...>
+arg_parity_extra <util> <extra-args...>        # optional
+arg_parity_case <util> "<args>" "<description>"  # optional, curated
+arg_parity_known <util> "<full_args>" "<reason>"   # optional, known mismatch
+```
+
+**Comparison modes:**
+
+| Mode | What's compared | Example utils |
+|---|---|---|
+| `stdout` | exit code + stdout + stderr (file as argument) | `ls`, `cat`, `sort`, `wc`, `stat`, `tail`, `uniq`, `du` |
+| `stdin` | exit code + stdout + stderr (piped input, no file arg) | `tr`, `echo` |
+| `filesystem` | exit code + stderr + resulting directory tree (src→dst) | `cp`, `mv`, `install`, `ln` |
+| `remove` | exit code + stderr + remaining tree (single arg, no dst) | `rm` |
+| `modify` | exit code + stderr + resulting metadata (extra+file) | `chmod` |
+
+**To add a flag:** append it to the `arg_parity_setup` line. Only add
+no-argument short flags — exclude flags that require arguments (like
+`-t DIR`), are dangerous to the testbed, produce non-deterministic output
+(`--color`), or block (`tail -f`).
+
+**To add a curated test case:** use `arg_parity_case` with a description.
+Curated cases run in addition to auto-generated singles + pairs.
+
+### `format-parity`
+
+Tests output format strings that other tools **parse**:
+
+| Section | What's tested | Integration at risk |
+|---|---|---|
+| `stat -c` format specifiers | All common specifiers (`%s`, `%a`, `%F`, `%u`, `%U`, `%g`, `%h`, `%i`, `%d`, `%t`, `%T`, `%m`, `%x`, `%y`, `%z`, `%w`, `%N`) against file, directory, and symlink. Also tests `stat -L` (dereference). | `x11-common` (exact-string match on `stat -c '%u %g %a %F'`), `screen-cleanup` (arithmetic on `stat -c%a`), initramfs (`stat -L -c %t:%T` for device major:minor), `fuse3.postinst` (`stat -c %d/%i` for container detection) |
+| `printf` format specifiers | `%s`, `%d`, `%x`, `%o`, `%f`, `%e`, `%g`, `%%`, `%5s`, `%-5s`, `%05d`, `%.3f`, `%c` | Shell scripts, initramfs cryptroot hook |
+| `printf` escape sequences | `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, `\r`, `\v`, `\f`, `\a`, `\0`, `%b` (backslash interpretation) | Shell scripts, NUL-separated pipelines |
+| `md5sum`/`sha256sum` output | Basic output, stdin, filename with spaces | `dh_md5sums` (assumes `hash  filename` format with backslash escaping) |
+
+**To add a test case:** add a `test_printf_format`/`test_printf_escape` call
+or a new `run_cmd` + `parity_compare` block.
+
+### `behavior-parity`
+
+Tests behavioral edge cases that system tools **assume**:
+
+| Section | What's tested | Integration at risk |
+|---|---|---|
+| `install` idiom | `install --mode NNN /dev/null FILE` (atomically create empty file with mode), `install -d` (directory creation), `install -D` (leading dirs + install) | Dozens of postinst scripts (apparmor, cups, man-db, etc.) via debhelper `postinst-apparmor` autoscript |
+| `realpath`/`readlink` | `realpath -m` (missing path), `-s` (no symlinks), `readlink -f`/`-e`/`-m` on symlinks, broken symlinks, directories, missing paths | initramfs-tools `hook-functions` (uses GNU-only `realpath -ms`) |
+| `tsort` | Linear, branching, disconnected, self-loop, empty input | initramfs-tools hook ordering (topological sort of prerequisites) |
+
+**To add a test case:** add a `test_install_idiom`/`test_realpath`/`test_readlink`/`test_tsort` call.
+
+### `pipeline-parity`
+
+Tests pipeline behavior:
+
+| Section | What's tested | Integration at risk |
+|---|---|---|
+| SIGPIPE handling | `yes \| head`, `seq \| head`, `cat /dev/zero \| head`, `dd \| head`, `sort \| head -n0` | Every pipeline in every shell script (LP #2134578, #2133156, #2125943) |
+| NUL-separated pipelines | `printf '%s\0' \| sort -z`, full `printf \| sort -z \| xargs -0 echo` pipeline | initramfs cryptroot, microcode hooks |
+
+**To add a test case:** add a `test_sigpipe`/`test_nul_pipeline`/`test_nul_full_pipeline` call.
+
+## FAIL (REDIRECTED) — testing GNU-redirected utils (all-utils)
+
+Some utils are currently redirected to GNU via the `coreutils-from-uutils`
+symlink layer (e.g. `cp → gnucp`, `df → gnudf`). The `all-utils` test
+still exercises the rust-coreutils version of these utils by running the
+binary at `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/<util>` directly.
+
+When a redirected util's smoke or functional test fails, it's reported as
+`FAIL (REDIRECTED)` — clearly distinguished from a regular `FAIL`:
+
+```
+PASS (REDIRECTED): cp        ← rust cp works, just isn't active yet
+FAIL (REDIRECTED): df ...     ← rust df has an issue (but doesn't fail the test)
+```
+
+`FAIL (REDIRECTED)` does **not** cause the test to fail (exit 1). Only
+failures on **active** rust-coreutils utils count as real failures.
+
+When a util is switched from GNU to rust-coreutils (by removing the
+redirect), the same failure automatically becomes a regular `FAIL` (exit 1)
+— no code changes needed. This means the test is always as strict as the
+current redirect configuration allows.
+
+## Known mismatches (known_issue / arg_parity_known)
+
+When a parity test finds a divergence between rust-coreutils and GNU
+coreutils, it reports a `MISMATCH` and the test **fails** (exit 1). This is
+intentional — divergences should be investigated, not silently ignored.
+
+Once a mismatch is triaged (either as expected behavior or linked to a
+Launchpad bug), it can be declared as a known issue:
+
+```sh
+# In arg-parity-data (for arg-parity test):
+arg_parity_known stat "-L" "GNU capitalizes 'Size:', rust uses 'size:'"
+
+# Or directly in the test script (for format-parity, behavior-parity, etc.):
+known_issue printf "'%%' ''" "GNU prints % then warning, rust prints warning then %"
+```
+
+Known mismatches are:
+- Still **reported** in the output (as `KNOWN MISMATCH` with the reason)
+- **Not counted** as failures — the test passes if all mismatches are known
+- **Visible** — the GNU and rust output is still shown side-by-side
+
+The `<full_args>` must match exactly what appears on the `MISMATCH:` line in
+the test output. To find the exact string, run the test and copy the args
+from the mismatch line.
+
+When a known mismatch is **fixed** in rust-coreutils, simply remove the
+`known_issue` / `arg_parity_known` line. If the fix is correct, the test
+will now pass without the known-issue exemption. If the fix introduces a
+new divergence, it will appear as a new `MISMATCH`.
+
+## GNU baseline comparison (system-build-sed)
+
+`system-build-sed` uses a conditional baseline comparison to attribute
+failures:
+
+1. Build sed without tests (`DEB_BUILD_OPTIONS=nocheck`)
+2. If the build fails → swap all `/usr/bin/<util>` symlinks to `gnu<util>`,
+   rebuild, and compare:
+   - GNU also fails → "sed bug, not coreutils-related"
+   - GNU succeeds → "rust-coreutils build regression"
+3. If the build succeeds → run `make check` with rust-coreutils
+4. If tests fail → swap to GNU, re-run `make check`, and compare:
+   - GNU also fails → "sed bug, not coreutils-related"
+   - GNU succeeds → "rust-coreutils regression"
+
+Symlink restoration is guaranteed via `trap ... EXIT`, so the testbed is
+always restored to rust-coreutils even on failure.
+
+This test requires `needs-root` + `isolation-machine` + `breaks-testbed`
+because it modifies system state (apt sources, `/usr/bin/` symlinks).
+
+## The `common` helpers
+
+Shared functions used by all tests:
+
+**Resolution & skip:**
+- `assert_rust_coreutils_active` — exits 77 (skip) if rust-coreutils is not
+  the active `/usr/bin/ls`. On releases still using GNU coreutils, all tests
+  skip cleanly.
+- `resolve_test_bin <util>` — resolves the binary path for a util, handling
+  GNU redirects (`cp → gnucp`, `df → gnudf`) and uutils-only utils
+  (`hashsum`, `sha3sum`).
+- `resolve_gnu_bin <util>` — resolves `/usr/bin/gnu<util>`.
+- `resolve_rust_bin <util>` — wraps `resolve_test_bin`, echoes the path.
+- `is_known_nonfunctional <util>` — returns true for utils that exist as
+  hardlinks but aren't real uutils programs (`relpath`, `hashsum`).
+
+**Parity testing (shared by all parity tests):**
+- `known_issue <util> "<args>" "<reason>"` — registers a known mismatch.
+- `check_known <util> <args>` — looks up whether a mismatch is known.
+- `report_mismatch <util> <args> <desc>` — classifies as KNOWN or MISMATCH,
+  increments the appropriate counter.
+- `mismatch_header <util> <args> <desc>` — prints the labeled header line.
+- `parity_compare <label> <util> <gnu_out> <rust_out> <gnu_rc> <rust_rc>` —
+  compares two outputs and reports PASS/MISMATCH.
+- `parity_summary` — prints the summary and exits with appropriate code.
+- `normalize_output <util> <text> <fix_path>` — removes implementation-specific
+  differences (program names, paths) before comparison.
+
+**System build tests:**
+- `preflight_coreutils_check <utils...>` — logs active binary path and version
+  for each util.
+- `save_symlinks` / `swap_to_gnu` / `restore_symlinks` — manage the
+  `/usr/bin/<util>` symlinks for baseline comparison.
+- `print_log_tail` / `grep_coreutils_in_log` / `save_artifact` — log
+  diagnostics for build tests.
+
+## How to run tests locally
+
+Most tests can be run directly (rust-coreutils must be installed and active
+as system coreutils):
+
+```sh
+AUTOPKGTEST_TMP=/tmp/adt debian/tests/all-utils
+AUTOPKGTEST_TMP=/tmp/adt debian/tests/arg-parity
+AUTOPKGTEST_TMP=/tmp/adt debian/tests/format-parity
+AUTOPKGTEST_TMP=/tmp/adt debian/tests/behavior-parity
+AUTOPKGTEST_TMP=/tmp/adt debian/tests/pipeline-parity
+AUTOPKGTEST_TMP=/tmp/adt debian/tests/regression-lp
+```
+
+`system-build-sed` requires root (for `apt-get source` + modifying apt
+sources) and is best run via autopkgtest with `isolation-machine`:
+
+```sh
+autopkgtest . -- qemu /path/to/image
+```
+
+## How to run via autopkgtest
+
+```sh
+# Run all tests
+autopkgtest . -- qemu /path/to/image
+
+# Run a specific test
+autopkgtest -a all-utils . -- qemu /path/to/image
+
+# Run with a local build
+autopkgtest -B . -- qemu /path/to/image
+```
+
+## Tips for maintainers
+
+- **When a new util is added to rust-coreutils.hardlinks:** it automatically
+  appears in `all-utils`. Add a functional test case to `all-utils-data` and
+  consider adding it to `arg-parity-data` with appropriate flags.
+
+- **When a new LP bug is fixed:** add a regression test to `regression-lp`
+  using the LP number in the test name and description.
+
+- **When `arg-parity` shows a new mismatch:** investigate whether it's a
+  rust-coreutils bug. If it is, file a bug and add `arg_parity_known` with
+  the LP number. If it's expected behavior, add `arg_parity_known` with a
+  description.
+
+- **When `format-parity`/`behavior-parity`/`pipeline-parity` shows a new
+  mismatch:** same workflow — investigate, and if expected, add a
+  `known_issue` call at the top of the script.
+
+- **When a known mismatch is fixed:** remove the `known_issue` /
+  `arg_parity_known` line. The test will now verify the fix works (the
+  mismatch should become a pass).
+
+- **When utils are switched from GNU to rust-coreutils** (like `cp` or
+  `df`): they automatically start being tested by `all-utils` and
+  `arg-parity` — no changes needed. The dynamic redirect detection handles
+  this.
+
+- **When adding a new integration area:** create a new `*-parity` script,
+  source `common`, use `parity_compare` for each test case, and call
+  `parity_summary` at the end. Add a stanza to `control` with
+  `@builddeps@, gnu-coreutils` dependencies.

+#!/bin/sh
+# all-utils: test every rust-coreutils utility.
+#
+# Phase 1: Resolution + smoke tests (generic, no per-util config)
+# Phase 2: Functional tests (from all-utils-data, human-edited)
+#
+# When a util is redirected to GNU (e.g. cp → gnucp), the rust-coreutils
+# version at /usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/<util> is still tested.
+# Failures on redirected utils are reported as FAIL (REDIRECTED) and do
+# not cause the test to fail — the util is redirected because it's not
+# ready yet. When the util is switched from GNU to rust, failures
+# automatically become regular FAIL (exit 1).
+#
+# See all-utils-data for how to add/modify functional test cases.
+
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+. debian/tests/all-utils-data
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+PASSED=0
+FAILED=0
+FAILED_REDIRECTED=0
+SKIPPED=0
+
+ALL_UTILS_ROOT="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-all-utils}/all-utils"
+mkdir -p "$ALL_UTILS_ROOT"
+
+# Parse util list from the hardlinks file installed by rust-coreutils.
+UTILS=$(awk '{print $2}' debian/rust-coreutils.hardlinks | sed 's|.*/coreutils/||' | sort -u)
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Phase 1: Resolution + smoke tests
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+smoke_version() {
+    local out rc
+    out=$("$1" --version 2>&1) || true
+    rc=$?
+    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && return 0
+    echo "$out" | grep -q "uutils coreutils" && return 0
+    return 1
+}
+
+smoke_help() {
+    local out rc
+    out=$("$1" --help 2>&1) || true
+    rc=$?
+    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && return 0
+    [ -n "$out" ] && return 0
+    return 1
+}
+
+echo "=== Phase 1: Resolution + smoke tests ==="
+for util in $UTILS; do
+    IS_GNU_REDIRECTED=0
+    bin=""
+
+    resolve_test_bin "$util"
+    case "$TEST_STATUS" in
+        rust|uutils-only)
+            bin="$TEST_BIN"
+            ;;
+        gnu-redirect)
+            # The util is redirected to GNU at /usr/bin/, but we can still
+            # test the rust-coreutils version directly.
+            rust_bin="/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/$util"
+            if [ -x "$rust_bin" ]; then
+                bin="$rust_bin"
+                IS_GNU_REDIRECTED=1
+            else
+                echo "SKIP: $util redirected to GNU, no rust binary found"
+                SKIPPED=$((SKIPPED + 1))
+                continue
+            fi
+            ;;
+        unexpected)
+            echo "FAIL: $util resolves to unexpected target: $TEST_BIN"
+            FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))
+            continue
+            ;;
+        missing)
+            echo "SKIP: $util binary not found"
+            SKIPPED=$((SKIPPED + 1))

+#!/bin/sh
+# arg-parity: compare rust-coreutils vs GNU coreutils for flag combinations.
+# Configuration is in arg-parity-data (sourced).
+#
+# For each util:
+#   1. Test all single flags from arg_parity_setup
+#   2. Test all pairwise combinations (both -aL combined and -a -L separate)
+#   3. Test curated cases from arg_parity_case
+# Compare by mode:
+#   stdout     → exit code + stdout + stderr (normalized)
+#   stdin      → exit code + stdout + stderr (piped input, no file arg)
+#   filesystem → exit code + stderr (normalized) + resulting directory tree
+#   remove     → exit code + stderr (normalized) + remaining tree after removal
+#   modify     → exit code + stderr (normalized) + resulting file metadata
+# Report all mismatches, then fail if any are unknown (not in arg_parity_known).
+
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+T="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-argparity}/arg-parity"
+mkdir -p "$T"
+
+PASSED=0
+MISMATCHED=0
+KNOWN=0
+TOTAL=0
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Storage for arg_parity_setup, arg_parity_case, and arg_parity_extra calls.
+# Must be defined BEFORE sourcing arg-parity-data.
+# Entries are newline-separated to avoid word-splitting on space-separated flags.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_ARG_PARITY_SETUP=""
+arg_parity_setup() {
+    local util="$1" mode="$2"
+    shift 2
+    local flags="$*"
+    _ARG_PARITY_SETUP="${_ARG_PARITY_SETUP}${_ARG_PARITY_SETUP:+
+}$util|$mode|$flags"
+}
+
+_ARG_PARITY_CASES=""
+arg_parity_case() {
+    _ARG_PARITY_CASES="${_ARG_PARITY_CASES}${_ARG_PARITY_CASES:+
+}$1|$2|$3"
+}
+
+_ARG_PARITY_EXTRA=""
+arg_parity_extra() {
+    local util="$1"
+    shift
+    _ARG_PARITY_EXTRA="${_ARG_PARITY_EXTRA}${_ARG_PARITY_EXTRA:+
+}$util|$*"
+}
+
+# arg_parity_known is an alias for the shared known_issue() from common.
+arg_parity_known() {
+    known_issue "$@"
+}
+
+# Source the data file (calls arg_parity_setup, arg_parity_case, etc.)
+. debian/tests/arg-parity-data
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Standard fixture: created fresh for each test case
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+create_fixture() {
+    local dir="$1"
+    rm -rf "$dir"
+    mkdir -p "$dir/dir"
+    printf 'hello\n' > "$dir/file.txt"
+    printf '' > "$dir/empty.txt"
+    printf 'nested\n' > "$dir/dir/nested.txt"
+    ln -s file.txt "$dir/link.txt"
+    ln -s nonexistent "$dir/broken.lnk"
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Capture directory tree state: type, mode, size, path, symlink target
+# (used by filesystem/remove/modify modes in this test only)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+capture_tree() {
+    local dir="$1"
+    ( cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null && find . -mindepth 1 -printf '%y %m %s %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort ) || true
+    ( cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null && find . -mindepth 1 -type l -printf '%p -> ' -exec readlink {} \; 2>/dev/null | sort ) || true
+    ( cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null && find . -mindepth 1 -type f -size -1k -printf '%p: ' -exec cat {} \; 2>/dev/null ) || true
+}
+
+# normalize_output, resolve_gnu_bin, resolve_rust_bin, check_known,
+# report_mismatch, mismatch_header, and counters are in common (sourced above).
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Run a single stdout-mode test case and compare results
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+run_stdout_case() {
+    local util="$1" args="$2" desc="$3"
+    local gnu_bin rust_bin
+    gnu_bin=$(resolve_gnu_bin "$util") || return 0
+    rust_bin=$(resolve_rust_bin "$util") || return 0
+
+    local fixture="$T/fixture"
+    create_fixture "$fixture"
+
+    # For stdout utils, use file.txt as the argument (not the directory)
+    local target="$fixture/file.txt"
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+    gnu_out=$("$gnu_bin" $args "$target" 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$("$rust_bin" $args "$target" 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    # Normalize: strip program name differences and path differences
+    gnu_out=$(normalize_output "$util" "$gnu_out" "$fixture")
+    rust_out=$(normalize_output "$util" "$rust_out" "$fixture")
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    if [ "$gnu_out" = "$rust_out" ] && [ "$gnu_rc" = "$rust_rc" ]; then
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    else
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$args" "$desc"
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$args" "$desc"
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, output=$gnu_out"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, output=$rust_out"
+    fi
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Run a single filesystem-mode test case and compare results
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+run_filesystem_case() {
+    local util="$1" args="$2" desc="$3"
+    local gnu_bin rust_bin
+    gnu_bin=$(resolve_gnu_bin "$util") || return 0
+    rust_bin=$(resolve_rust_bin "$util") || return 0
+
+    local gnu_fix="$T/gnu_fix" rust_fix="$T/rust_fix"
+    local gnu_dst="$T/gnu_dst" rust_dst="$T/rust_dst"
+
+    create_fixture "$gnu_fix/src"
+    create_fixture "$rust_fix/src"
+    rm -rf "$gnu_dst" "$rust_dst"
+
+    local gnu_err gnu_rc rust_err rust_rc
+    gnu_err=$("$gnu_bin" $args "$gnu_fix/src" "$gnu_dst" 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_err=$("$rust_bin" $args "$rust_fix/src" "$rust_dst" 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    # Normalize stderr
+    gnu_err=$(normalize_output "$util" "$gnu_err" "$gnu_fix")
+    rust_err=$(normalize_output "$util" "$rust_err" "$rust_fix")
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" != "$rust_rc" ]; then
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$args" "$desc"
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$args" "$desc"
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, stderr=$gnu_err"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, stderr=$rust_err"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if [ "$gnu_err" != "$rust_err" ]; then
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$args" "$desc"
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$args" "$desc"

+    rust_tree=$(capture_tree "$rust_dst" 2>/dev/null)

+        mismatch_header "$util" "$args" "$desc"

+        echo "$gnu_tree" | sed 's/^/    /'
+        echo "  RUST tree:"

+# Passes a single fixture argument, then compares exit code + stderr +

+    rust_err=$("$rust_bin" $args "$rust_fix/src" 2>&1); rust_rc=$?

+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" != "$rust_rc" ]; then

+        mismatch_header "$util" "$args" "$desc"

+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, stderr=$rust_err"

+        echo "  RUST: stderr=$rust_err"

+        mismatch_header "$util" "$args" "$desc"

+        echo "$gnu_tree" | sed 's/^/    /'
+        echo "  RUST remaining:"
+        echo "$rust_tree" | sed 's/^/    /'

+

+}

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Run a single stdin-mode test case and compare results.
+# Pipes a fixed string to the command, no file argument.
+# Extra args (from arg_parity_extra) are appended after flags.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+run_stdin_case() {
+    local util="$1" args="$2" desc="$3" is_curated="${4:-no}"

+'

+    create_fixture "$gnu_fix/src"
+    create_fixture "$rust_fix/src"

+
+    gnu_err=$(normalize_output "$util" "$gnu_err" "$gnu_fix")
+    rust_err=$(normalize_output "$util" "$rust_err" "$rust_fix")
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" != "$rust_rc" ]; then
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$full_args" "$desc"
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$full_args" "$desc"
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, stderr=$gnu_err"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, stderr=$rust_err"

+    fi
+
+    if [ "$gnu_err" != "$rust_err" ]; then
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$full_args" "$desc"
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$full_args" "$desc"
+        echo "  GNU:  stderr=$gnu_err"
+        echo "  RUST: stderr=$rust_err"

+    rust_tree=$(capture_tree "$rust_fix/src" 2>/dev/null)

+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Look up extra args for a util from _ARG_PARITY_EXTRA.
+# Echoes the extra args string, or empty if none.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+lookup_extra() {
+    local util="$1"
+    local result
+    result=$(echo "$_ARG_PARITY_EXTRA" | while IFS='|' read -r e_util e_extra; do
+        [ -z "$e_util" ] && continue
+        if [ "$e_util" = "$util" ]; then
+            echo "$e_extra"
+            break
+        fi
+    done)
+    echo "$result"
+}
+
+# check_known, report_mismatch, mismatch_header are in common (sourced above).
+# Echoes "mode|flags" or returns 1 if not found.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+lookup_setup() {
+    local util="$1"
+    local result
+    result=$(echo "$_ARG_PARITY_SETUP" | while IFS='|' read -r e_util e_mode e_flags; do
+        [ -z "$e_util" ] && continue
+        if [ "$e_util" = "$util" ]; then
+            echo "$e_mode|$e_flags"
+            break
+        fi
+    done)
+    [ -z "$result" ] && return 1
+    echo "$result"
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Run all test cases for a single util
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+run_util() {
+    local util="$1"
+    local setup
+    setup=$(lookup_setup "$util")
+    if [ -z "$setup" ]; then
+        echo "SKIP: $util has no arg_parity_setup"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    local mode flags
+    mode=$(echo "$setup" | cut -d'|' -f1)
+    flags=$(echo "$setup" | cut -d'|' -f2)
+
+    local flag_count
+    flag_count=$(echo "$flags" | wc -w)
+    echo "=== $util ($mode mode, $flag_count flags) ==="
+    local runner
+    case "$mode" in
+        stdout)     runner="run_stdout_case" ;;
+        stdin)      runner="run_stdin_case" ;;
+        filesystem) runner="run_filesystem_case" ;;
+        remove)     runner="run_remove_case" ;;
+        modify)     runner="run_modify_case" ;;
+        *)          echo "ERROR: unknown mode '$mode' for $util"; return ;;
+    esac
+
+    # 1. All single flags
+    for f in $flags; do
+        $runner "$util" "-$f" ""
+    done
+
+    # 2. All pairs (combined form -f1f2 and separate form -f1 -f2)
+    local seen=""
+    for f1 in $flags; do
+        for f2 in $flags; do
+            [ "$f1" = "$f2" ] && continue
+            local pair1="$f1$f2" pair2="$f2$f1"
+            if echo "$seen" | grep -qF "$pair2"; then
+                continue
+            fi
+            seen="$seen $pair1"
+            $runner "$util" "-$f1$f2" ""
+            $runner "$util" "-$f1 -$f2" ""
+        done
+    done
+
+    # 3. Curated cases
+    echo "$_ARG_PARITY_CASES" | while IFS='|' read -r c_util c_args c_desc; do
+        [ -z "$c_util" ] && continue
+        [ "$c_util" = "$util" ] || continue
+        $runner "$util" "$c_args" "$c_desc" "yes"
+    done
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Main
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== arg-parity: comparing rust-coreutils vs GNU coreutils ==="
+echo ""
+
+for util in $ARG_PARITY_UTILS; do
+    run_util "$util"
+    echo ""
+done
+
+parity_summary

+# arg-parity-data: per-util configuration for arg-parity test.

+#   2. Call arg_parity_setup with its safe flags and comparison mode
+#   3. (Optional) Call arg_parity_extra if the util needs fixed extra args

+#   4. (Optional) Add curated test cases with arg_parity_case
+#
+# HOW TO ADD A FLAG:
+#   Just append it to the arg_parity_setup line for that util.
+#   Only add no-argument short flags. Exclude flags that require arguments
+#   (like -t DIR), are dangerous to the testbed, produce non-deterministic
+#   output (--color), or are SELinux-related.
+#
+# HOW TO ADD A CURATED TEST CASE:
+#   arg_parity_case <util> "<args>" "<description>"

+#   Curated cases run in addition to auto-generated singles + pairs.

+#   Known mismatches are reported but do not cause test failure.
+#   To find the exact <full_args> for a mismatch, run arg-parity and copy
+#   the args from the "MISMATCH:" line.
+#
+# COMPARISON MODES:
+#   stdout     — compare exit code + stdout + stderr (file as argument)
+#   stdin      — compare exit code + stdout + stderr (piped input, no file arg)
+#   filesystem — compare exit code + stderr + resulting directory tree (src→dst)

+#   For modify mode: inserted before the file (e.g. chmod -R 755 file → 755 is extra)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+#!/bin/sh
+# behavior-parity: compare rust-coreutils vs GNU for behavioral edge cases.
+#
+# Tests integration assumptions made by system tools:
+#   - install --mode NNN /dev/null FILE (conffile seeding idiom in postinst)
+#   - install -d, install -D, install -t (directory creation patterns)
+#   - realpath -m / -s (GNU-only flags used by initramfs-tools)
+#   - readlink -f / -e / -m (canonical path resolution)
+#   - tsort (topological sort used by initramfs hook ordering)
+
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+T="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-behavior-parity}/behavior-parity"
+mkdir -p "$T"
+
+GNU_INSTALL=$(resolve_gnu_bin install || true)
+RUST_INSTALL=$(resolve_test_bin install && echo "$TEST_BIN" || true)
+GNU_REALPATH=$(resolve_gnu_bin realpath || true)
+RUST_REALPATH=$(resolve_test_bin realpath && echo "$TEST_BIN" || true)
+GNU_READLINK=$(resolve_gnu_bin readlink || true)
+RUST_READLINK=$(resolve_test_bin readlink && echo "$TEST_BIN" || true)
+GNU_TSORT=$(resolve_gnu_bin tsort || true)
+RUST_TSORT=$(resolve_test_bin tsort && echo "$TEST_BIN" || true)
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 1: install idiom parity
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== install idiom parity ==="
+
+# The "install --mode NNN /dev/null FILE" idiom: atomically create an empty
+# file with a specific mode. Used in dozens of postinst scripts.
+test_install_idiom() {
+    local mode="$1"
+    local gnu_file="$T/gnu_idiom_$mode"
+    local rust_file="$T/rust_idiom_$mode"
+    rm -f "$gnu_file" "$rust_file"
+
+    local gnu_rc rust_rc
+    "$GNU_INSTALL" --mode "$mode" /dev/null "$gnu_file" 2>&1; gnu_rc=$?
+    "$RUST_INSTALL" --mode "$mode" /dev/null "$rust_file" 2>&1; rust_rc=$?
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" = "$rust_rc" ] && [ -f "$gnu_file" ] && [ -f "$rust_file" ]; then
+        # Compare permissions
+        local gnu_perm rust_perm
+        gnu_perm=$(stat -c %a "$gnu_file" 2>/dev/null)
+        rust_perm=$(stat -c %a "$rust_file" 2>/dev/null)
+        if [ "$gnu_perm" = "$rust_perm" ]; then
+            PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+        else
+            MISMATCHED=$((MISMATCHED + 1))
+            echo "MISMATCH: install --mode $mode /dev/null FILE"
+            echo "  GNU:  file exists, perm=$gnu_perm"
+            echo "  RUST: file exists, perm=$rust_perm"
+        fi
+    else
+        report_mismatch "install" "--mode $mode /dev/null FILE" ""
+        mismatch_header "install" "--mode $mode /dev/null FILE" ""
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, file exists=$([ -f "$gnu_file" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, file exists=$([ -f "$rust_file" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
+    fi
+}
+
+test_install_idiom 644
+test_install_idiom 755
+test_install_idiom 600
+test_install_idiom 640
+
+# install -d (create directory)
+test_install_d() {
+    local label="install -d $1"
+    local gnu_dir="$T/gnu_d_$(echo "$1" | tr '/' '_')"
+    local rust_dir="$T/rust_d_$(echo "$1" | tr '/' '_')"
+    rm -rf "$gnu_dir" "$rust_dir"
+
+    local gnu_rc rust_rc
+    "$GNU_INSTALL" -d "$gnu_dir" 2>&1; gnu_rc=$?
+    "$RUST_INSTALL" -d "$rust_dir" 2>&1; rust_rc=$?
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" = "$rust_rc" ] && [ -d "$gnu_dir" ] && [ -d "$rust_dir" ]; then
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    else
+        report_mismatch "install" "$label" ""
+        mismatch_header "install" "$label" ""
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, dir exists=$([ -d "$gnu_dir" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, dir exists=$([ -d "$rust_dir" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
+    fi
+}
+
+test_install_d "$T/deep/nested/dir"
+test_install_d "$T/a/b/c/d/e"
+
+# install -D (create leading dirs + install file)
+test_install_D() {
+    local label="install -D src dst"
+    local src="$T/install_src"
+    local gnu_dst="$T/gnu/deep/path/dst"
+    local rust_dst="$T/rust/deep/path/dst"
+    printf 'content\n' > "$src"
+    rm -rf "$T/gnu" "$T/rust"
+
+    local gnu_rc rust_rc
+    "$GNU_INSTALL" -D "$src" "$gnu_dst" 2>&1; gnu_rc=$?
+    "$RUST_INSTALL" -D "$src" "$rust_dst" 2>&1; rust_rc=$?
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" = "$rust_rc" ] && [ -f "$gnu_dst" ] && [ -f "$rust_dst" ]; then
+        # Compare content
+        if [ "$(cat "$gnu_dst")" = "$(cat "$rust_dst")" ]; then
+            PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+        else
+            MISMATCHED=$((MISMATCHED + 1))
+            echo "MISMATCH: $label (content differs)"
+            echo "  GNU:  $(cat "$gnu_dst")"
+            echo "  RUST: $(cat "$rust_dst")"
+        fi
+    else
+        report_mismatch "install" "$label" ""
+        mismatch_header "install" "$label" ""
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, file exists=$([ -f "$gnu_dst" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, file exists=$([ -f "$rust_dst" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
+    fi
+}
+
+test_install_D
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 2: realpath / readlink edge cases
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo ""
+echo "=== realpath / readlink parity ==="
+
+# realpath -m (canonicalize missing paths — GNU-only, used by initramfs)
+test_realpath() {
+    local flags="$1" path="$2" label="$3"
+    [ -z "$GNU_REALPATH" ] || [ -z "$RUST_REALPATH" ] && return 0
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+    gnu_out=$("$GNU_REALPATH" $flags "$path" 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$("$RUST_REALPATH" $flags "$path" 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    gnu_out=$(echo "$gnu_out" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+    rust_out=$(echo "$rust_out" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "realpath" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+# realpath -m on a nonexistent path (initramfs depends on this)
+test_realpath -m "$T/nonexistent/deep/path/file" "realpath -m (missing path)"
+test_realpath -ms "$T/nonexistent/deep/path/file" "realpath -ms (missing, no symlinks)"
+test_realpath -s "$T/file.txt" "realpath -s (no symlinks)"
+test_realpath "" "$T/file.txt" "realpath (basic)"
+test_realpath "" "$T/link.txt" "realpath (symlink deref)"
+
+# /proc/self paths are inherently non-comparable: the PID differs between
+# the GNU and rust processes. Skip these.
+
+# readlink -f / -e / -m on various paths
+test_readlink() {
+    local flags="$1" path="$2" label="$3"
+    [ -z "$GNU_READLINK" ] || [ -z "$RUST_READLINK" ] && return 0
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+    gnu_out=$("$GNU_READLINK" $flags "$path" 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$("$RUST_READLINK" $flags "$path" 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    gnu_out=$(echo "$gnu_out" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+    rust_out=$(echo "$rust_out" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "readlink" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+# Create a symlink for testing
+ln -sf "$T/file.txt" "$T/symlink_to_file"
+ln -sf "$T/nonexistent" "$T/broken_symlink"
+mkdir -p "$T/realdir"
+
+test_readlink -f "$T/symlink_to_file" "readlink -f (symlink)"
+test_readlink -f "$T/broken_symlink" "readlink -f (broken symlink)"
+test_readlink -f "$T/realdir" "readlink -f (directory)"
+test_readlink -f "$T/nonexistent" "readlink -f (nonexistent)"
+test_readlink -e "$T/symlink_to_file" "readlink -e (existing symlink)"
+test_readlink -e "$T/broken_symlink" "readlink -e (broken symlink)"
+test_readlink -m "$T/nonexistent/deep" "readlink -m (missing path)"
+
+# /proc/self tests are inherently non-comparable: the PID and /proc/self/exe
+# differ between the GNU and rust processes. Skip these.
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 3: tsort parity
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo ""
+echo "=== tsort parity ==="
+
+test_tsort() {
+    local input="$1" label="$2"
+    [ -z "$GNU_TSORT" ] || [ -z "$RUST_TSORT" ] && return 0
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+    gnu_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | "$GNU_TSORT" 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | "$RUST_TSORT" 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "tsort" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+# Linear graph
+test_tsort "a b
+b c
+c d" "linear graph"
+
+# Branching graph

+a c
+b d
+c d" "branching graph"
+
+# Disconnected components
+test_tsort "a b
+c d" "disconnected components"
+
+# Single node (self-loop is a cycle)
+test_tsort "a a" "self-loop"
+
+# Empty input
+test_tsort "" "empty input"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Summary
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+parity_summary

+# Common helpers for rust-coreutils autopkgtests.
+# This file is sourced, not executed.
+
+# Force C locale so both GNU and rust-coreutils produce identical
+# locale-dependent output (error messages, sorting, dates, etc.).
+# Without this, GNU uses smart quotes in error messages under UTF-8 locales.
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+# Skip (exit 77) if rust-coreutils is not the active system coreutils.
+# On systems still using GNU coreutils as /usr/bin/*, these tests are
+# not relevant and should be skipped cleanly.
+assert_rust_coreutils_active() {
+    local target
+    target=$(readlink -f /usr/bin/ls 2>/dev/null || true)
+    case "$target" in
+        */cargo/bin/coreutils/*)
+            return 0
+            ;;
+        *)
+            echo "SKIP: rust-coreutils is not the active coreutils (/usr/bin/ls -> ${target:-none})"
+            exit 77
+            ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# Resolve the test binary for a given util name.
+# Sets TEST_BIN to the path to use, or sets TEST_BIN="" and returns 1
+# if the util should be skipped (GNU redirect, not found, etc.).
+# Also sets TEST_STATUS to one of: rust, gnu-redirect, uutils-only, missing, unexpected
+resolve_test_bin() {
+    local util="$1"
+    local bin="/usr/bin/$util"
+    local rust_bin="/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/$util"
+
+    TEST_BIN=""
+    TEST_STATUS=""
+
+    if [ -L "$bin" ]; then
+        local target
+        target=$(readlink -f "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true)
+        case "$target" in
+            */cargo/bin/coreutils/*)
+                TEST_BIN="$bin"
+                TEST_STATUS="rust"
+                return 0
+                ;;
+            *gnu*)
+                TEST_STATUS="gnu-redirect"
+                return 1
+                ;;
+            *)
+                TEST_STATUS="unexpected"
+                TEST_BIN="$target"
+                return 1
+                ;;
+        esac
+    elif [ -x "$rust_bin" ]; then
+        TEST_BIN="$rust_bin"
+        TEST_STATUS="uutils-only"
+        return 0
+    else
+        TEST_STATUS="missing"
+        return 1
+    fi
+}
+
+# Check if a util is a known non-functional program (exists as a hardlink
+# but not a real uutils utility).
+is_known_nonfunctional() {
+    case "$1" in
+        relpath|hashsum)
+            return 0
+            ;;
+        *)
+            return 1
+            ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# Print the active binary path and version for each named util.
+# Usage: preflight_coreutils_check mktemp mkdir cp mv ...
+# Output goes to stdout; caller should redirect to a log file.
+preflight_coreutils_check() {
+    echo "=== Coreutils pre-flight check ==="
+    echo "Date: $(date 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
+    echo "Kernel: $(uname -r 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
+    echo ""
+    for util in "$@"; do
+        local bin="/usr/bin/$util"
+        local gnu_bin="/usr/bin/gnu$util"
+        local rust_bin="/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/$util"
+        local target version
+
+        if [ -L "$bin" ]; then
+            target=$(readlink -f "$bin" 2>/dev/null || echo "broken")
+            version=$("$bin" --version 2>&1 | head -n1 || echo "(no version)")
+        elif [ -x "$rust_bin" ]; then
+            target="$rust_bin (uutils-only, not in /usr/bin)"
+            version=$("$rust_bin" --version 2>&1 | head -n1 || echo "(no version)")
+        elif [ -x "$gnu_bin" ]; then
+            target="$gnu_bin (GNU only)"
+            version=$("$gnu_bin" --version 2>&1 | head -n1 || echo "(no version)")
+        else
+            target="not found"
+            version="(missing)"
+        fi
+
+        printf '%-12s -> %-50s %s\n' "$util" "$target" "$version"
+    done
+    echo ""
+}
+
+# Save the current symlink targets for all /usr/bin/<util> entries
+# that are managed by coreutils-from-uutils.
+# Usage: save_symlinks <output_file>
+save_symlinks() {
+    local out="$1"
+    : > "$out"
+    local util
+    for util in $(dpkg -L coreutils-from-uutils 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^/usr/bin/' | sed 's|.*/||' | sort); do
+        local link="/usr/bin/$util"
+        if [ -L "$link" ]; then
+            local target
+            target=$(readlink "$link" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+            if [ -n "$target" ]; then
+                echo "$util $target" >> "$out"
+            fi
+        fi
+    done
+}
+
+# Swap all coreutils-from-uutils symlinks to point to gnu<util>.
+# Requires gnu-coreutils package to be installed.
+swap_to_gnu() {
+    local util
+    for util in $(dpkg -L coreutils-from-uutils 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^/usr/bin/' | sed 's|.*/||' | sort); do
+        local link="/usr/bin/$util"
+        local gnu_bin="/usr/bin/gnu$util"
+        if [ -L "$link" ] && [ -x "$gnu_bin" ]; then
+            ln -sf "gnu$util" "$link"
+        fi
+    done
+}
+
+# Restore symlinks from a file saved by save_symlinks.
+# Usage: restore_symlinks <input_file>
+restore_symlinks() {
+    local in="$1"
+    [ -f "$in" ] || return 0
+    while read -r util target; do
+        [ -n "$util" ] && [ -n "$target" ] || continue
+        ln -sf "$target" "/usr/bin/$util" 2>/dev/null || true
+    done < "$in"
+}
+
+# Print the last N lines of a log file with a header.
+# Usage: print_log_tail <file> <n> <label>
+print_log_tail() {
+    local file="$1" n="$2" label="$3"
+    echo ""
+    echo "=== Last $n lines of $label ($file) ==="
+    if [ -f "$file" ]; then
+        tail -n "$n" "$file"
+    else
+        echo "(log file not found)"
+    fi
+    echo "=== end of $label ==="
+}
+
+# Search a log file for coreutils util names and print matches.
+# Usage: grep_coreutils_in_log <file>
+grep_coreutils_in_log() {
+    local file="$1"
+    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
+    local utils="mktemp mkdir rmdir install cp mv rm ln link unlink chmod chown \
+chgrp touch truncate shred cat tac head tail cut paste tr sort uniq wc nl fold \
+expand unexpand comm join csplit split tsort od fmt pr ptx basename dirname \
+pwd readlink realpath pathchk dd seq yes factor stat du sum cksum md5sum \
+sha1sum sha256sum sha512sum b2sum base32 base64 basenc echo printf test expr \
+date numfmt shuf ls dir vdir dircolors env printenv whoami id groups hostid \
+logname users who pinky uname nproc arch tty nice nohup sleep timeout stdbuf \
+true false sync"
+    echo ""
+    echo "=== Coreutils util names found in $file ==="
+    grep -inE "\b($(echo "$utils" | tr ' ' '|'))\b" "$file" | head -n 30 || echo "(none found)"
+    echo "=== end of grep ==="
+}
+
+# Save a file to $AUTOPKGTEST_ARTIFACTS if set.
+# Usage: save_artifact <file>
+save_artifact() {
+    local file="$1"
+    if [ -n "${AUTOPKGTEST_ARTIFACTS:-}" ] && [ -d "$AUTOPKGTEST_ARTIFACTS" ] && [ -f "$file" ]; then
+        cp "$file" "$AUTOPKGTEST_ARTIFACTS/" 2>/dev/null || true
+    fi
+}
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Parity testing helpers (used by arg-parity, format-parity, behavior-parity,
+# pipeline-parity). These provide the known-issues mechanism so that
+# expected divergences can be excused without failing the test.
+# ===========================================================================
+
+# Counters — initialized to 0. Sourcing scripts may reset these.
+PASSED=0
+MISMATCHED=0
+KNOWN=0
+TOTAL=0
+
+# Storage for known issues (newline-separated "util|args|reason").
+_KNOWN_ISSUES=""
+
+# Register a known mismatch.
+# Usage: known_issue <util> "<full_args>" "<reason>"
+# Use "LP: #XXXXXX" in the reason to link a Launchpad bug.
+known_issue() {
+    _KNOWN_ISSUES="${_KNOWN_ISSUES}${_KNOWN_ISSUES:+
+}$1|$2|$3"
+}
+
+# Check if a mismatch is a known issue.
+# Echoes the reason string if known, or empty if not.
+# Usage: check_known <util> <display_args>
+check_known() {
+    local util="$1" display_args="$2"
+    echo "$_KNOWN_ISSUES" | while IFS='|' read -r k_util k_args k_reason; do
+        [ -z "$k_util" ] && continue
+        if [ "$k_util" = "$util" ] && [ "$k_args" = "$display_args" ]; then
+            echo "$k_reason"
+            break
+        fi
+    done
+}
+
+# Classify a mismatch as KNOWN or unknown, increment the appropriate counter.
+# Sets _MISMATCH_LABEL and _MISMATCH_REASON.
+# Usage: report_mismatch <util> <display_args> <desc>
+report_mismatch() {
+    local util="$1" display_args="$2" desc="$3"
+    local reason
+    reason=$(check_known "$util" "$display_args")
+    if [ -n "$reason" ]; then
+        KNOWN=$((KNOWN + 1))
+        _MISMATCH_LABEL="KNOWN MISMATCH"
+        _MISMATCH_REASON="$reason"
+    else
+        MISMATCHED=$((MISMATCHED + 1))
+        _MISMATCH_LABEL="MISMATCH"
+        _MISMATCH_REASON=""
+    fi
+}
+
+# Print the mismatch header line (after report_mismatch).
+# Usage: mismatch_header <util> <display_args> <desc>
+mismatch_header() {
+    local util="$1" display_args="$2" desc="$3"
+    echo "$_MISMATCH_LABEL: $util $display_args  $( [ -n "$desc" ] && echo "($desc)" )"
+    [ -n "$_MISMATCH_REASON" ] && echo "  Known issue: $_MISMATCH_REASON"
+}
+
+# Resolve the GNU binary for a util (e.g. /usr/bin/gnuls).
+# Echoes the path or returns 1.
+resolve_gnu_bin() {
+    local util="$1"
+    local gnu="/usr/bin/gnu$util"
+    if [ -x "$gnu" ]; then
+        echo "$gnu"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    return 1
+}
+
+# Resolve the rust-coreutils binary for a util.
+# Echoes the path or returns 1.
+resolve_rust_bin() {
+    local util="$1"
+    resolve_test_bin "$util" || return 1
+    echo "$TEST_BIN"
+}
+
+# Normalize output: remove implementation-specific differences.
+#   - Replace gnu<util> with <util> in program names
+#   - Replace fixture paths with placeholders
+# Usage: normalize_output <util> <text> <fix_path>
+normalize_output() {
+    local util="$1" text="$2" fix_path="$3"
+    text=$(echo "$text" | sed "s/gnu$util\\>/$util/g")
+    text=$(echo "$text" | sed "s|/usr/bin/gnu$util\\>|$util|g")
+    text=$(echo "$text" | sed "s|/usr/bin/$util\\>|$util|g")
+    text=$(echo "$text" | sed "s|$fix_path|<FIXTURE>|g")
+    text=$(echo "$text" | sed "s|${fix_path%/*}/gnu_dst|<DST>|g; s|${fix_path%/*}/rust_dst|<DST>|g")
+    echo "$text"
+}
+
+# Compare GNU vs rust output for a parity test case.
+# Usage: parity_compare <label> <util> <gnu_out> <rust_out> <gnu_rc> <rust_rc>
+# Reports PASS/KNOWN MISMATCH/MISMATCH and increments counters.
+parity_compare() {
+    local label="$1" util="$2" gnu_out="$3" rust_out="$4" gnu_rc="$5" rust_rc="$6"
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    if [ "$gnu_out" = "$rust_out" ] && [ "$gnu_rc" = "$rust_rc" ]; then
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    else
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$label" ""
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$label" ""
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, output=$gnu_out"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, output=$rust_out"
+    fi
+}
+
+# Print the parity test summary and exit.
+parity_summary() {
+    echo ""
+    echo "=== Summary ==="
+    echo "Total:     $TOTAL"
+    echo "PASS:      $PASSED"
+    echo "KNOWN:     $KNOWN"
+    echo "MISMATCH:  $MISMATCHED"
+    echo ""
+    [ "$MISMATCHED" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
+}

+#!/bin/sh
+# format-parity: compare rust-coreutils vs GNU for output format strings.
+#
+# Tests that tools which PARSE coreutils output depend on:
+#   - stat -c format specifiers (used by x11-common, screen-cleanup, initramfs)
+#   - printf format specifiers and escape sequences (used by shell scripts)
+#   - md5sum/sha256sum output format (used by dh_md5sums, dpkg)
+#
+# A format divergence here means a script that parses the output will
+# silently break. This is the most fragile integration surface.
+
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+T="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-format-parity}/format-parity"
+mkdir -p "$T"
+
+# Resolve binaries once
+GNU_STAT=$(resolve_gnu_bin stat || true)
+RUST_STAT=$(resolve_rust_bin stat || true)
+GNU_PRINTF=$(resolve_gnu_bin printf || true)
+RUST_PRINTF=$(resolve_rust_bin printf || true)
+GNU_MD5SUM=$(resolve_gnu_bin md5sum || true)
+RUST_MD5SUM=$(resolve_rust_bin md5sum || true)
+GNU_SHA256SUM=$(resolve_gnu_bin sha256sum || true)
+RUST_SHA256SUM=$(resolve_rust_bin sha256sum || true)
+
+# Create standard test files
+printf 'hello\n' > "$T/file.txt"
+printf '' > "$T/empty.txt"
+mkdir -p "$T/dir"
+ln -s file.txt "$T/link.txt"
+
+# Helper: run a command and capture output + exit code
+# Usage: run_cmd <bin> <args...>
+# Sets _OUT and _RC
+run_cmd() {
+    _OUT=$("$@" 2>&1) || true
+    _RC=$?
+}
+
+# Like run_cmd, but pipes output directly to od -c to preserve NUL bytes.
+# Shell $(...) strips NUL bytes from variables, so run_cmd can't capture
+# them. This helper avoids that by piping the command's output directly to
+# od without going through a variable.
+# Sets _OD_OUT and _OD_RC.
+# Usage: run_printf_od <bin> <args...>
+run_printf_od() {
+    _OD_OUT=$({ "$@" 2>&1; echo $? > "$T/_rc"; } | od -c)
+    _OD_RC=$(cat "$T/_rc" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 1: stat -c format specifiers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== stat format specifiers ==="
+
+[ -z "$GNU_STAT" ] || [ -z "$RUST_STAT" ] && echo "SKIP: stat binary not found" || true
+
+# Format specifiers tested against a regular file, directory, and symlink
+STAT_FORMATS="%s %n %F %a %A %u %U %g %G %h %i %d %t %T %x %y %z %w %m %N"
+
+for fmt in $STAT_FORMATS; do
+    for target_name in file.txt dir link.txt; do
+        target="$T/$target_name"
+        label="stat -c '$fmt' $target_name"
+
+        run_cmd "$GNU_STAT" -c "$fmt" "$target"
+        gnu_out=$(echo "$_OUT" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+        gnu_rc=$_RC
+
+        run_cmd "$RUST_STAT" -c "$fmt" "$target"
+        rust_out=$(echo "$_OUT" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+        rust_rc=$_RC
+
+        parity_compare "$label" "stat" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+    done
+done
+
+# stat -L (dereference) on the symlink
+for fmt in $STAT_FORMATS; do
+    label="stat -L -c '$fmt' link"
+    run_cmd "$GNU_STAT" -L -c "$fmt" "$T/link.txt"
+    gnu_out=$(echo "$_OUT" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+    gnu_rc=$_RC
+
+    run_cmd "$RUST_STAT" -L -c "$fmt" "$T/link.txt"
+    rust_out=$(echo "$_OUT" | sed "s|$T|<FIXTURE>|g")
+    rust_rc=$_RC
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "stat" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+done
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 2: printf format specifiers and escape sequences
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo ""
+echo "=== printf format specifiers ==="
+
+[ -z "$GNU_PRINTF" ] || [ -z "$RUST_PRINTF" ] && echo "SKIP: printf binary not found" || true
+
+# Format specifiers with a sample argument
+# Format: specifier|argument
+test_printf_format() {
+    fmt="$1"
+    arg="$2"
+    label="printf '$fmt' '$arg'"
+
+    run_cmd "$GNU_PRINTF" "$fmt" "$arg"
+    gnu_out=$_OUT
+    gnu_rc=$_RC
+
+    run_cmd "$RUST_PRINTF" "$fmt" "$arg"
+    rust_out=$_OUT
+    rust_rc=$_RC
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "printf" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+test_printf_format '%s' 'hello'
+test_printf_format '%d' '42'
+test_printf_format '%i' '42'
+test_printf_format '%o' '42'
+test_printf_format '%x' '255'
+test_printf_format '%X' '255'
+test_printf_format '%f' '3.14'
+test_printf_format '%e' '3.14'
+test_printf_format '%g' '3.14'
+test_printf_format '%%' ''
+test_printf_format '%5s' 'hi'
+test_printf_format '%-5s' 'hi'
+test_printf_format '%05d' '42'

@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+#!/bin/sh
+# pipeline-parity: compare rust-coreutils vs GNU for pipeline behavior.
+#
+# Tests:
+#   - SIGPIPE handling: commands in pipelines where the downstream command
+#     exits early. This is where tee/sort/dd/yes broken pipe bugs live.
+#   - NUL-separated pipelines: printf '%s\0' | sort -z | xargs -0
+#     Used by initramfs cryptroot and microcode hooks.
+
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+T="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-pipeline-parity}/pipeline-parity"
+mkdir -p "$T"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 1: SIGPIPE handling
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== SIGPIPE handling ==="
+
+# Test that commands in pipelines don't crash when downstream exits early.
+# We compare exit codes and stderr between GNU and rust-coreutils.
+# The upstream command should exit 0 (or at least not crash with a signal).
+
+test_sigpipe() {
+    local label="$1" util="$2"
+    local gnu_bin rust_bin
+    gnu_bin=$(resolve_gnu_bin "$util") || return 0
+    rust_bin=$(resolve_rust_bin "$util") || return 0
+
+    shift 2
+    # Remaining args are the pipeline after the util
+    local pipeline="$@"
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+
+    # Run with GNU coreutils
+    gnu_out=$(yes | "$gnu_bin" $pipeline 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    # Run with rust-coreutils
+    rust_out=$(yes | "$rust_bin" $pipeline 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    # For SIGPIPE tests, we care that the command doesn't crash with a signal.
+    # Exit codes may differ (GNU uses 141 for SIGPIPE, rust may use 0 or 1).
+    # We check that neither produces a core dump or unexpected error.
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" -lt 128 ] && [ "$rust_rc" -lt 128 ]; then
+        # Both exited normally (no signal)
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    elif [ "$gnu_rc" -ge 128 ] && [ "$rust_rc" -ge 128 ]; then
+        # Both got a signal (likely SIGPIPE=13, so exit 141)
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    else
+        # One got a signal, the other didn't — potential divergence
+        report_mismatch "$util" "$label" ""
+        mismatch_header "$util" "$label" ""
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc, output=$gnu_out"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc, output=$rust_out"
+    fi
+}
+
+# yes | head -n1 — classic SIGPIPE trigger
+test_sigpipe "yes | head -n1" yes head -n1
+
+# seq | head -n1
+test_sigpipe "seq | head -n1" seq head -n1
+
+# cat /dev/zero | head -c1
+test_sigpipe "cat /dev/zero | head -c1" cat head -c1
+
+# dd | head — had broken pipe bug (LP #2125943)
+test_sigpipe "dd | head" dd bs=1 count=100 head -c1
+
+# sort | head -n0 — had broken pipe bug (LP #2133156)
+# For this we need input to sort
+test_sort_sigpipe() {
+    local gnu_sort rust_sort gnu_head rust_head
+    gnu_sort=$(resolve_gnu_bin sort) || return 0
+    rust_sort=$(resolve_rust_bin sort) || return 0
+    gnu_head=$(resolve_gnu_bin head) || return 0
+    rust_head=$(resolve_rust_bin head) || return 0
+
+    local gnu_rc rust_rc
+    printf '1\n2\n3\n' | "$gnu_sort" | "$gnu_head" -n0 >/dev/null 2>&1; gnu_rc=$?
+    printf '1\n2\n3\n' | "$rust_sort" | "$rust_head" -n0 >/dev/null 2>&1; rust_rc=$?
+
+    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
+    # sort may exit non-zero due to SIGPIPE, but shouldn't crash
+    if [ "$gnu_rc" -lt 128 ] && [ "$rust_rc" -lt 128 ]; then
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    elif [ "$gnu_rc" -ge 128 ] && [ "$rust_rc" -ge 128 ]; then
+        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
+    else
+        report_mismatch "sort" "sort | head -n0 (LP #2133156)" ""
+        mismatch_header "sort" "sort | head -n0 (LP #2133156)" ""
+        echo "  GNU:  exit=$gnu_rc"
+        echo "  RUST: exit=$rust_rc"
+    fi
+}
+
+test_sort_sigpipe
+
+# echo | sort | head — compound pipeline
+test_compound_pipeline() {
+    local label="$1"
+    local gnu_sort rust_sort gnu_head rust_head
+    gnu_sort=$(resolve_gnu_bin sort) || return 0
+    rust_sort=$(resolve_rust_bin sort) || return 0
+    gnu_head=$(resolve_gnu_bin head) || return 0
+    rust_head=$(resolve_rust_bin head) || return 0
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+    gnu_out=$(printf 'c\na\nb\n' | "$gnu_sort" | "$gnu_head" -n1 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$(printf 'c\na\nb\n' | "$rust_sort" | "$rust_head" -n1 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "sort" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+test_compound_pipeline "echo | sort | head -n1"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Section 2: NUL-separated pipelines
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo ""
+echo "=== NUL-separated pipeline parity ==="
+
+# Test that NUL-separated pipelines work identically.
+# Used by initramfs cryptroot and microcode hooks:
+#   printf '%s\0' a b c | sort -z | xargs -0 echo
+
+test_nul_pipeline() {
+    local label="$1" input="$2"
+    local gnu_sort rust_sort gnu_xargs rust_xargs
+    gnu_sort=$(resolve_gnu_bin sort) || return 0
+    rust_sort=$(resolve_rust_bin sort) || return 0
+    # xargs is not coreutils, but the pipeline behavior depends on sort -z
+    # producing correct NUL-separated output
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+
+    # Build NUL-separated input and pipe through sort -z
+    # Then convert back to newline-separated for comparison
+    gnu_out=$(printf "$input" | "$gnu_sort" -z 2>&1 | tr '\0' '\n'); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$(printf "$input" | "$rust_sort" -z 2>&1 | tr '\0' '\n'); rust_rc=$?
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "sort" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+# NUL-separated sort
+test_nul_pipeline "sort -z (3 items)" 'c\0a\0b\0'
+test_nul_pipeline "sort -z (5 items)" 'e\0c\0a\0b\0d\0'
+test_nul_pipeline "sort -z (1 item)" 'a\0'
+test_nul_pipeline "sort -z (empty)" ''
+
+# NUL-separated printf → sort -z → xargs -0 pipeline
+test_nul_full_pipeline() {
+    local label="$1"
+    local gnu_sort rust_sort gnu_xargs rust_xargs
+    gnu_sort=$(resolve_gnu_bin sort) || return 0
+    rust_sort=$(resolve_rust_bin sort) || return 0
+
+    local gnu_out gnu_rc rust_out rust_rc
+
+    # printf '%s\0' b a c | sort -z | xargs -0 echo
+    gnu_out=$(printf 'b\0a\0c\0' | "$gnu_sort" -z 2>/dev/null | xargs -0 echo 2>&1); gnu_rc=$?
+    rust_out=$(printf 'b\0a\0c\0' | "$rust_sort" -z 2>/dev/null | xargs -0 echo 2>&1); rust_rc=$?
+
+    parity_compare "$label" "sort" "$gnu_out" "$rust_out" "$gnu_rc" "$rust_rc"
+}
+
+test_nul_full_pipeline "printf %s\\0 | sort -z | xargs -0 echo"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Summary
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+parity_summary

+#!/bin/sh
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+T="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-regression}/regression-lp"
+mkdir -p "$T"
+
+FAILED=0
+
+fail() {
+    echo "FAIL: $1"
+    FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))
+}
+
+pass() {
+    echo "PASS: $1"
+}
+
+# LP: #2134578 - tee with multiple --append fails
+test_tee_multiple_append() {
+    printf 'a\nb\n' > "$T/tee_in"
+    printf 'x\n' > "$T/tee_file"
+    if printf 'a\nb\n' | tee -a -a "$T/tee_file" | grep -q 'a' \
+       && [ "$(wc -l < "$T/tee_file")" = "3" ]; then
+        pass "LP #2134578: tee with multiple --append"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2134578: tee with multiple --append"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2132150 - dd: O_DIRECT partial block writes fail
+# We test basic dd with small block sizes (O_DIRECT needs a block device,
+# which is not available in autopkgtest, but we test the general path)
+test_dd_partial_writes() {
+    if dd if=/dev/zero of="$T/dd_out" bs=1 count=10 2>/dev/null \
+       && [ "$(wc -c < "$T/dd_out")" = "10" ]; then
+        pass "LP #2132150: dd partial block writes"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2132150: dd partial block writes"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2125504 - sort -k option does not behave as GNU's sort
+test_sort_k_option() {
+    printf '3 c\n1 a\n2 b\n' | sort -k1 -n > "$T/sort_out"
+    if [ "$(head -n1 "$T/sort_out" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "1" ] \
+       && [ "$(tail -n1 "$T/sort_out" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "3" ]; then
+        pass "LP #2125504: sort -k field semantics"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2125504: sort -k field semantics"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2132941 - env: Rust unwrap with UTF-8 symbols in environment variables
+test_env_utf8() {
+    out=$(env 'FOO=café' env | grep '^FOO=' || true)
+    if echo "$out" | grep -q 'café'; then
+        pass "LP #2132941: env UTF-8 in environment variables"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2132941: env UTF-8 in environment variables"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2130859 - date does not support localized output
+test_date_localized() {
+    if LC_ALL=C date +%Y 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^[0-9]\{4\}$'; then
+        pass "LP #2130859: date localized output"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2130859: date localized output"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2141441 - autopkgtest failures in resolute due to readlink
+test_readlink_proc() {
+    # readlink -f /proc/self should resolve to /proc/<pid>
+    if readlink -f /proc/self 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^/proc/[0-9]\+$'; then
+        pass "LP #2141441: readlink -f /proc/self"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2141441: readlink -f /proc/self"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2138315 - comm does not work as expected with process substitution
+# Test with temp files (process substitution is bash-specific)
+test_comm_files() {
+    printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > "$T/comm1"
+    printf 'a\nc\nd\n' > "$T/comm2"
+    out=$(comm "$T/comm1" "$T/comm2")
+    # Column 1 (only in file1): b
+    # Column 2 (only in file2): d
+    # Column 3 (in both): a, c
+    if echo "$out" | grep -q 'b' && echo "$out" | grep -q 'd' \
+       && echo "$out" | grep -q 'a'; then
+        pass "LP #2138315: comm with file arguments"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2138315: comm with file arguments"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2132245 - du is double-counting hard links when multiple arguments specified
+test_du_hardlinks() {
+    printf 'data\n' > "$T/du_orig"
+    ln "$T/du_orig" "$T/du_link" 2>/dev/null || true
+    # du with hardlinks should not double-count when given both paths
+    # Just verify du runs without error and produces a number
+    if du -s "$T/du_orig" "$T/du_link" 2>/dev/null | tail -n1 | grep -q '^[0-9]'; then
+        pass "LP #2132245: du with hardlinks"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2132245: du with hardlinks"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2125943 - rust-coreutils:dd: Broken pipe
+test_dd_broken_pipe() {
+    # dd should not crash when its output pipe is closed early
+    if yes | dd bs=1 count=1 2>/dev/null | head -c1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        pass "LP #2125943: dd broken pipe"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2125943: dd broken pipe"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2133156 - echo 1 | sort | head -n0: sort: write failed: Broken pipe
+test_sort_broken_pipe() {
+    # sort should handle SIGPIPE gracefully when downstream closes early.
+    # sort may exit 141 (SIGPIPE) or 0, but must not crash with a different
+    # signal (e.g. SIGABRT=134). Capture sort's exit code via a subshell
+    # that writes it to a file, since PIPESTATUS is not available in sh.
+    rm -f "$T/sort_rc"
+    ( echo 1 | sort; echo $? > "$T/sort_rc" ) 2>/dev/null | head -n0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    rc=$(cat "$T/sort_rc" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
+    if [ "$rc" -lt 128 ] || [ "$rc" -eq 141 ]; then
+        pass "LP #2133156: sort broken pipe with head -n0"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2133156: sort broken pipe with head -n0 (exit $rc)"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2127851 - rust-coreutils stats handling breaks wireguard's wg-quick
+# Test that stat format strings work correctly
+test_stat_formats() {
+    touch "$T/stat_file"
+    if stat -c '%s' "$T/stat_file" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^[0-9]\+$' \
+       && stat -c '%n' "$T/stat_file" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '.' \
+       && stat -c '%F' "$T/stat_file" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '.'; then
+        pass "LP #2127851: stat format strings"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2127851: stat format strings"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2142588 - date: gnu date allows options after format
+test_date_options_after_format() {
+    # date should allow options like -d after the format string
+    out=$(date -d @0 +%Y 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [ "$out" = "1970" ]; then
+        pass "LP #2142588: date options after format"
+    else
+        fail "LP #2142588: date options after format (got: $out)"
+    fi
+}
+
+# LP: #2130396 - rust-coreutils 'shred' refuses to write to a device
+# Skip: requires a block device, not available in autopkgtest
+test_shred_device() {
+    echo "SKIP: LP #2130396: shred on device (requires block device)"
+}
+
+# LP: #2122166 - uutils wc crashed with SIGABRT on logout
+# Skip: requires logout/session end scenario, not reproducible in autopkgtest
+test_wc_sigabrt() {
+    echo "SKIP: LP #2122166: wc SIGABRT on logout (requires session end scenario)"
+}
+
+# --- Run all tests ---
+
+test_tee_multiple_append
+test_dd_partial_writes
+test_sort_k_option
+test_env_utf8
+test_date_localized
+test_readlink_proc
+test_comm_files
+test_du_hardlinks
+test_dd_broken_pipe
+test_sort_broken_pipe
+test_stat_formats
+test_date_options_after_format
+test_shred_device
+test_wc_sigabrt
+
+echo ""
+echo "=== Regression Summary ==="
+echo "FAILED: $FAILED"
+
+[ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

+#!/bin/sh
+set -u
+
+. debian/tests/common
+assert_rust_coreutils_active
+
+T="${AUTOPKGTEST_TMP:-/tmp/adt-sed}"
+mkdir -p "$T"
+SYMLINKS_SAVE="$T/symlinks.save"
+APT_SOURCES_BACKUP="$T/apt-sources.backup"
+LOG_BUILD="$T/build.log"
+LOG_TEST_RUST="$T/test-rust.log"
+LOG_TEST_GNU="$T/test-gnu.log"
+LOG_PREFLIGHT="$T/preflight.log"
+
+# Restore symlinks and apt sources on exit — even if the script is killed
+# (SIGTERM, OOM, timeout). The testbed may be reused by autopkgtest, so
+# leaving /usr/bin/* pointed at GNU or deb-src enabled would affect
+# subsequent runs.
+restore_state() {
+    if [ -d "$APT_SOURCES_BACKUP" ]; then
+        cp "$APT_SOURCES_BACKUP"/*.sources /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ 2>/dev/null || true
+    fi
+    restore_symlinks "$SYMLINKS_SAVE" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+trap restore_state EXIT INT TERM
+
+# Key coreutils utils that sed's build/test suite is likely to use.
+KEY_UTILS="mktemp mkdir rmdir install cp mv rm ln chmod cat echo printf test \
+expr cut sort head tail wc dd touch basename dirname readlink realpath pwd \
+tr tee fold expand unexpand seq stat du od split csplit comm join tsort fmt \
+uniq nl pathchk factor sum cksum env printenv true false sleep"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Phase 0: Pre-flight diagnostic
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== Phase 0: Pre-flight diagnostic ==="
+preflight_coreutils_check $KEY_UTILS > "$LOG_PREFLIGHT" 2>&1
+cat "$LOG_PREFLIGHT"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Phase 0b: Enable deb-src and fetch sed source + build deps
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== Phase 0b: Fetching sed source ==="
+mkdir -p "$APT_SOURCES_BACKUP"
+for f in /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.sources; do
+    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
+    cp "$f" "$APT_SOURCES_BACKUP/"
+    sed -i 's/^Types: deb$/Types: deb deb-src/' "$f"
+done
+apt-get update -qq
+
+cd "$T"
+apt-get source sed
+apt-get build-dep -y sed
+
+srcdir=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'sed-*' | head -n1)
+if [ -z "$srcdir" ]; then
+    echo "FAIL: could not find extracted sed source directory"
+    exit 1
+fi
+echo "sed source: $srcdir"
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Phase 1: Build sed (without tests)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+echo "=== Phase 1: Building sed (no tests) with rust-coreutils ==="
+cd "$T/$srcdir"
+if DEB_BUILD_OPTIONS=nocheck dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b -j"$(nproc)" \
+        > "$LOG_BUILD" 2>&1; then
+    echo "PASS: sed built successfully"
+    save_artifact "$LOG_BUILD"
+else
+    BUILD_RC=$?
+    echo "FAIL: sed build failed (exit $BUILD_RC) with rust-coreutils"
+    print_log_tail "$LOG_BUILD" 100 "build.log"
+    grep_coreutils_in_log "$LOG_BUILD"
+    save_artifact "$LOG_BUILD"
+    save_artifact "$LOG_PREFLIGHT"
+
+    # Baseline: try building with GNU coreutils
+    echo ""
+    echo "=== Baseline: rebuilding sed with GNU coreutils ==="
+    save_symlinks "$SYMLINKS_SAVE"
+    swap_to_gnu
+    echo "Swapped $(wc -l < "$SYMLINKS_SAVE") symlinks to GNU coreutils"
+
+    cd "$T/$srcdir"
+    rm -f "$T"/sed_*.deb
+    if DEB_BUILD_OPTIONS=nocheck dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b -j"$(nproc)" \
+            > "$T/build-gnu.log" 2>&1; then
+        echo "BASELINE PASS: sed builds with GNU coreutils but not rust-coreutils"
